checked_markdown_lines: Building Structures Illustrated (2nd Edition): Live loads are moving or movable loads created by occupancy, collected water or snow, and movable equipment or objects. Locator: Building Structures Illustrated refined markdown lines 2077-2133 and 2872-2876

Building Structures Illustrated (2nd Edition): Distributed and concentrated loading differ in how load reaches the spanning system. Locator: Building Structures Illustrated refined markdown lines 2077-2133 and 2872-2876

Building Construction Illustrated (5th Edition): Floor and roof systems support dead, live, and lateral loads; rigid floor planes can act as diaphragms that transfer lateral forces to shear walls. Locator: Building Construction Illustrated refined markdown lines 720, 2107-2143, 4149-4153, and 4189-4197

Building Construction Illustrated (5th Edition): Earthquakes can move a building base suddenly and induce shaking in all directions, with horizontal components treated as most important in structural design. Locator: Building Construction Illustrated refined markdown lines 720, 2107-2143, 4149-4153, and 4189-4197

Building Construction Illustrated (5th Edition): Under earthquake loading, building mass develops inertial force as it resists horizontal ground acceleration. Locator: Building Construction Illustrated refined markdown lines 720, 2107-2143, 4149-4153, and 4189-4197

Building Construction Illustrated (5th Edition): Heavy buildings can resist wind overturning by weight but are susceptible to larger earthquake inertial forces. Locator: Building Construction Illustrated refined markdown lines 720, 2107-2143, 4149-4153, and 4189-4197

Dynamics of Structures: Theory and Applications to Earthquake Engineering: A strong-motion accelerograph records three components of earthquake ground shaking and is triggered by arriving earthquake waves. Locator: Dynamics of Structures refined markdown lines 11592-11608, 11711-11713, 12096-12110, 12183-12185, and 12315-12331

Dynamics of Structures: Theory and Applications to Earthquake Engineering: Accelerographs must be maintained and serviced so they produce a record when shaking occurs. Locator: Dynamics of Structures refined markdown lines 11592-11608, 11711-11713, 12096-12110, 12183-12185, and 12315-12331

Dynamics of Structures: Theory and Applications to Earthquake Engineering: Acceleration-time records can be integrated to velocity and displacement, but baseline and triggering issues affect accuracy. Locator: Dynamics of Structures refined markdown lines 11592-11608, 11711-11713, 12096-12110, 12183-12185, and 12315-12331

Dynamics of Structures: Theory and Applications to Earthquake Engineering: Peak base shear relates to structure weight and pseudo-acceleration through a base shear or lateral force coefficient. Locator: Dynamics of Structures refined markdown lines 11592-11608, 11711-11713, 12096-12110, 12183-12185, and 12315-12331

Dynamics of Structures: Theory and Applications to Earthquake Engineering: Response spectra organize peak deformation, pseudo-velocity, and pseudo-acceleration response over vibration periods and damping levels. Locator: Dynamics of Structures refined markdown lines 11592-11608, 11711-11713, 12096-12110, 12183-12185, and 12315-12331
